records.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.

content.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of adjunctive therapies for proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) related to rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from January 2000 to December 2025. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was used to compare different therapies.

Results

A total of 2,519 patients from 18 RCTs were included (1,339 receiving adjunctive treatments and 1,180 receiving placebo). Oral retinoic acid was associated with significantly higher primary (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.86, 95% CI = [1.16, 7.53]) and final (HR = 2.90, 95% CI = [1.12, 7.50]) retinal reattachment rates, improved visual acuity (MD=-0.89, 95% CI = [-1.68, -0.08]), and a lower incidence of postoperative macular pucker (HR = 0.12, 95% CI = [0.02, 0.50]) compared with placebo. Oral prednisolone had a lower rate of PVR recurrence compared with placebo (HR = 0.37, 95% CI = [0.17, 0.79]), while oral retinoic acid (HR = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.00, 0.50]) and intravitreal dexamethasone (HR = 0.23, 95% CI = [0.05, 0.81]) were associated with reduced rates of RRD reoperation.

Conclusion

Oral retinoic acid ranked highest for primary outcomes in PVR associated with RRD; however, this finding was driven by a single RCT with limited sample size. Oral prednisolone reduced PVR recurrence, while intravitreal dexamethasone lowered reoperation risk, compared with placebo.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Complementary Value of Biomarkers for Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Complementary Value of Biomarkers for Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the individual and combined diagnostic performance of cytokine, molecular, and clonality biomarkers for primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Participants

A total of 2411 patients from 41 studies with confirmed PVRL or benign ocular inflammatory diseases.

Methods

Prospectively registered (CRD420251265910). Four databases were searched through November 25, 2025. Methodologic quality was assessed using QUADAS-2 and Comparative tools. Diagnostic accuracy was pooled using hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) models with GRADE certainty assessment.

Main outcome measures

Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and AUSROC for each biomarker with GRADE certainty ratings.

Results

Of 41 included studies, most were rated at high or unclear risk of bias across Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 domains, predominantly in patient selection because of retrospective designs and nonconsecutive sampling, and in the index test domain because of post hoc threshold selection. The interleukin (IL)-10 to IL-6 ratio (27 studies; 1370 patients; AUSROC, 0.98; sensitivity, 0.89; specificity, 0.98; I2 = 61% and 69%, respectively; low certainty) showed no publication bias. MYD88 (12 studies; 382 patients; AUSROC, 0.89; sensitivity, 0.73, specificity, 0.99; I2 = 37% and 68%, respectively; very low certainty), IGH (12 studies; 649 patients; AUSROC, 0.97; sensitivity, 0.85, specificity, 0.97; I2 = 80% and 87%, respectively; very low certainty), and IL-10 alone (11 studies; 549 patients; AUSROC, 0.94; sensitivity, 0.87, specificity, 0.95; I2 = 58% and 84%, respectively; low certainty) did not outperform IL-10 and IL-6 statistically. CD79B (4 studies; 123 patients; AUSROC, 1.00; sensitivity, 0.40; specificity, 1.00; I2 = 35% and 0%, respectively; low certainty) showed numerically higher accuracy (P = 0.055). Parallel testing of IL-10 to IL-6 ratio and MYD88 achieved 97.1% sensitivity and 97.0% specificity, reducing false-negative rates from 11% to 2.9%.

Conclusions

Parallel testing of IL-10 to IL-6 ratio and MYD88 seemed to offer the highest diagnostic performance among evaluated strategies for PVRL, although this finding requires prospective validation given the low to very low certainty of the underlying evidence. Aqueous humor cytokine testing yielded higher diagnostic odds ratios than vitreous fluid, suggesting anterior paracentesis for IL-10 to IL-6 ratio before vitreous biopsy for molecular confirmation.

Financial disclosure(s)

The author(s) have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

records.title: Intraocular Pressure Changes Following Intraluminal Stent Removal From the Paul Glaucoma Implant: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Intraocular Pressure Changes Following Intraluminal Stent Removal From the Paul Glaucoma Implant: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to systematically review and perform a single-arm meta-analysis to comprehensively evaluate the effect of removal of intraluminal stent from the Paul glaucoma implant (PGI) on intraocular pressure (IOP) changes and to summarize its long-term efficacy and safety.

Clinical relevance

Glaucoma remains one of the leading global causes of irreversible vision loss, necessitating effective surgical management for refractory cases. Glaucoma drainage devices are critical for these complex forms, and intraluminal stent removal from the PGI serves as a key strategy to titrate aqueous outflow and optimize long-term IOP control.

Methods

A systematic review was conducted by searching EMBASE, Medline, and CENTRAL. The meta-analysis ultimately included 5 observational studies. The Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool was used to assess the quality of the included studies. Continuous outcomes (eg, postremoval stent IOP reduction) were analyzed using the mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); dichotomous outcomes (eg, hypotony incidence) were evaluated using pooled proportion with 95% CI. All meta-analyses employed a random-effects model.

Results

Our meta-analysis included 5 studies, involving a total of 283 eyes. The meta-analysis revealed that removal of the stent leads to a significant and immediate IOP reduction. The IOP reduction (immediate postremoval stent IOP minus preremoval stent IOP) was significant, with a pooled MD of -9.09 mm Hg IOP (MD = 9.09; 95% CI = [-11.77, -6.41]). In the preremoval stent high-IOP (>21 mm Hg) subgroup, the IOP reduction is -11.82 (95% CI = [-10.14, -13.51]). This reduction was significantly greater than the preremoval stent low-IOP (<21 mm Hg) subgroup, whose reduction is -6.66 mm Hg (95% CI = [-5.55, -7.77]). Regarding safety, the pooled proportion of clinically hypotony was low and highly consistent (I² = 0.00%) at only 0.03 (95% CI = [0.00, 0.15]).

Conclusions

Intraluminal stent removal from the PGI is an effective and safe IOP-lowering intervention. Its IOP reduction effect is significantly more pronounced in patients with preremoval stent high IOP, providing crucial clinical guidance for managing persistently high IOP after PGI implantation.

records.title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AND ENDOPHTHALMITIS AFTER INTRAVITREAL INJECTION: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AND ENDOPHTHALMITIS AFTER INTRAVITREAL INJECTION: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the incidence of endophthalmitis after intravitreal injection with versus without topical antibiotic prophylaxis.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from each database's inception through August 2024. The primary outcome measure was the endophthalmitis rates after intravitreal injection, whereas the secondary outcomes included the distribution and quantity of microorganisms and best-corrected visual acuity changes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For the meta-analysis, pooled summary estimates were calculated using a random-effects model.

Results

Eighteen studies (3,138,778 intravitreal injections; 1,426 endophthalmitis cases) showed no significant difference in endophthalmitis incidence between prophylaxis and no-prophylaxis groups (odds ratio 1.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72‒4.76; P = 0.2). For microbial analysis, we selected 11 studies that demonstrated no significant difference in culture-positive rates between prophylaxis and nonprophylaxis groups (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, [0.53‒2.84]; P = 0.63). Four studies provided best-corrected visual acuity changes from baseline to final follow-up, antibiotic prophylaxis group showed a decrease by 4.5 ETDRS letters compared with the no-prophylaxis group, although this difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.65).

Conclusion

Topical antibiotics did not reduce endophthalmitis risk or improve visual outcomes postintravitreal injection. Given potential risks, routine prophylaxis is not recommended.

records.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to integrate the clinical and multimodal imaging features of extensive macular atrophy associated with pseudodrusen (EMAP), and to evaluate its progression and associated risk factors.

Clinical relevance

EMAP is a retinal disorder with a distinct phenotype and poor visual prognosis that typically affects patients in their middle age. There is no standardized classification for EMAP nor a clear understanding of its etiology. Identifying clinical and imaging biomarkers is critical to improve EMAP diagnosis and guiding future research.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO, CRD42024474924). A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov was performed up to June 19, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies of EMAP were eligible. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic, and risk of bias by the NOS. The examined outcomes were disease symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), progression of macular atrophy, imaging biomarkers, and systemic associations. EMAP was diagnosed using multimodal imaging analysis.

Results

Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria for qualitative analysis, and 12 datasets were included (N = 1096 eyes). The mean BCVA at diagnosis was 0.62 logMAR (95% CI: 0.47-0.76; I² = 95.6%), with a mean worsening of 0.41 logMAR (3 lines of vision) over 2.1 years. Disease progression involved an increase in the macular atrophy area by an average of 8.3 mm² over 3.9 years (95% CI: 3-3.57; I² = 69.8%). Optical coherence tomography showed a mean central choroidal thickness of 135.8 (95% CI: 113.3-158.3; I² = 94.4%). Electroretinography data indicated a rod dysfunction with abnormal photopic response. Rheumatic fever was reported in 89% of patients across Brazilian cohorts (95% CI: 83.2-93; I² = 0%).

Conclusions

This meta-analysis has limitations, mostly due to heterogeneity and biases inherent to non-randomized studies of this disease, hence the inconsistencies in the results and hypothesized associations underlying EMAP. Despite the different imaging modalities used to diagnose EMAP, the results demonstrate the common features that characterize and support its diagnosis.

records.title: Rate and Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy with Semaglutide Use for Diabetes and Weight Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Rate and Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy with Semaglutide Use for Diabetes and Weight Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the rate and risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in adults receiving semaglutide for diabetes or weight loss.

Clinical relevance

Semaglutide is a transformative treatment for diabetes and obesity. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is a serious cause of sudden, often permanent, vision loss. A comprehensive synthesis of available and conflicting evidence of a potential link is needed to inform clinical practice.

Methods

Our comprehensive search included MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, clinical trial registries, and direct contact with trial sponsors to identify unpublished data from inception to March 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating semaglutide versus placebo or standard therapy in adults. Incident NAION was the primary outcome. Pooled incidence rates, hazard ratios (HRs), and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models, uniquely stratified by both clinical indication (diabetes/weight loss) and study design.

Results

Our search identified 8 RCTs (31 174 patients, including 3 RCTs not previously synthesized in meta-analyses) and 8 observational studies (1 611 278 patients) were included. Observational studies for diabetes showed a pooled NAION incidence of 26.7 per 100 000 person-years in those on semaglutide versus 18.9 per 100 000 person-years in those not on semaglutide (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.20-2.85). Randomized controlled trials for diabetes demonstrated 5 ischemic optic neuropathy events in those on semaglutide versus one in those not, with no significant evidence of increased risk (RR 1.76, 95% CI 0.43-7.25). Observational studies of semaglutide for weight loss showed no evidence of increased NAION hazards (HR 1.57, 95% CI 0.69-3.59), and RCTs (4 ION events vs one) found no evidence of increased risk (RR 2.18, 95% CI 0.33-14.34).

Conclusion

The absolute rate of NAION in semaglutide users is low. Our novel, stratified analysis provides a more nuanced interpretation than previous pooled reviews, isolating a potential increased risk signal to observational data in the diabetes population only, a finding not corroborated by RCTs. The comprehensiveness of our search and rigorous sensitivity analyses to account for patient overlap in databases strengthen the validity of these conclusions. This synthesis highlights the need for continued pharmacovigilance while contextualizing the low absolute risk.

records.title: Fibrin Glue Versus Sutures for Securing Conjunctival Autograft in Primary Pterygium Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Fibrin Glue Versus Sutures for Securing Conjunctival Autograft in Primary Pterygium Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether fibrin glue provides superior outcomes compared to sutures for securing conjunctival autografts in primary pterygium surgery. We focused on recurrence rates, operative time, postoperative complications, and patient discomfort.

Clinical relevance

Pterygium recurrence and postoperative morbidity remain significant concerns in ocular surface surgery. A growing number of surgeons are adopting fibrin glue instead of sutures to anchor conjunctival autografts, but the evidence on comparative effectiveness has evolved in recent years. This updated analysis aims to guide surgical practice with the most current data.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL on 8 November 2024. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing fibrin glue versus sutures in primary pterygium surgery. Studies were screened, selected, and data-extracted by two independent reviewers. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024520625).

Results

Twenty RCTs were included. Fibrin glue significantly reduced recurrence risk compared to sutures (pooled odds ratio: 2.46; 95% CI: 1.06-5.69; 27 P  =  .0352; I2 = 0%). Operative time was significantly shorter with fibrin glue (pooled mean difference: 15.65 29 minutes; 95% CI: 11.45-19.86; P < .005; I2 = 99.29%). Pain scores at postoperative day 1 were significantly lower with fibrin glue compared with sutures (pooled standardized mean difference: 1.32; 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.52; p < .001; I2 = 90%). Rates of graft retraction were inconsistent between the two groups, while subconjunctival hemorrhages were more common in the suture group.

Conclusion

Fibrin glue is associated with lower recurrence rates, reduced operative time, and less postoperative discomfort than sutures in primary pterygium surgery. However, variability in graft retraction outcomes warrants further investigation. These findings support the broader adoption of fibrin glue as a preferred technique for conjunctival autograft fixation in routine clinical practice.

records.title: Clinical Efficacy of Biosimilar Switch of Adalimumab and Infliximab for Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Clinical Efficacy of Biosimilar Switch of Adalimumab and Infliximab for Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the clinical efficacy of switching from originator tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitors to biosimilars in the management of noninfectious uveitis.

Design

A systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted on PubMed, Embase, and Scopus according to PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251051301). Studies were included if they reported outcomes related to uveitis control, including flare frequency, oral corticosteroid use, or nonbiologic immunomodulatory therapy (IMT) use, before and after switching. Meta-analyses were performed to compare the incidence rate ratio (IRR) of uveitis flares, as well as the risk ratios (RR) of oral corticosteroid and nonbiological IMT use, before and after switching.

Results

A total of 6 studies were included, with publication dates ranging from 2019 to 2024. The studies included a total of 202 patients that underwent an originator to biosimilar switch. The pooled IRR of uveitis flares postswitch was 1.26 (95% CI: 0.72-2.21, P = 0.411), with significant heterogeneity (P = 0.08). Heterogeneity could be resolved through a secondary analysis excluding flares occurring within 3 months postswitch, due to early flare clustering reported in 1 study, that found an IRR of 1.20 (95% CI: 0.79-1.83, P = 0.388) without heterogeneity (P = .25). There was no significant change in the risk of oral steroid use (RR = 1.00; 95% CI: 0.88-1.12, P = 0.944) or nonbiologic IMT use (RR = 0.98; 95% CI 0.83-1.16, P = .858) postswitch. A total of 30 patients (Pooled Proportions = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.041-0.219, P = 0.022) reverted to the originator agent, most commonly due to injection-site pain or technical difficulties with the biosimilar injector.

Conclusions

Switching from originator to biosimilar TNF-α inhibitors in noninfectious uveitis was not associated with an increase in flare rates, supporting the clinical equivalence of these biosimilars. However, a subset of patients may experience tolerability issues or early flares, warranting close monitoring in the months following a switch.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Deep learning for multimodal depression detection: A review.
records.publisher: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

content.title: Deep learning for multimodal depression detection: A review.
content.abstract: Depression is a critical global public health challenge, yet its diagnosis still relies heavily on subjective self-report scales. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled objective, quantitative assessment through multimodal data fusion, including text, audio, and visual behaviors. Although multimodal approaches consistently outperform unimodal methods, the field lacks a systematic review that synthesizes these developments within a unified comparative framework. To address this gap, this paper provides a comprehensive review of deep learning-based multimodal depression detection. We first summarize clinical foundations and benchmark datasets. We then trace the evolution of feature extraction methods, from hand-crafted representations to modern Foundation Models and Large Language Models (LLMs). Furthermore, we categorize advanced fusion strategies, such as cross-modal alignment, dual-modality interaction, and trimodal joint modeling, and establish a horizontal comparison across model families to analyze trade-offs in performance, computational cost, and robustness. Finally, we identify common failure modes, including noise propagation and domain generalization gaps, and outline future research directions toward reliable and clinically applicable systems.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: Mapping the Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in Pneumonia Research: A Bibliometric Analysis (2016-2025).

content.title: Mapping the Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in Pneumonia Research: A Bibliometric Analysis (2016-2025).
content.abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of the Artificial intelligence-pneumonia literature, a comprehensive bibliometric mapping of this field has been lacking. To address this gap, this bibliometric study systematically maps the global research landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in pneumonia, based on 3,523 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoS). Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace for co-authorship, co-occurrence, co-citation, and burst detection, we found that annual output grew from 20 to 725 papers and citations from 12 to 19,503 between 2016 and 2025, with a marked acceleration after 2020. China dominated in publication volume, followed by the United States and India, yet the United Kingdom and Australia achieved substantially higher citations per paper, revealing a productivity-impact divide. International collaboration was intensive, particularly between China and the US. Thematic evolution shifted from early work on radiation pneumonitis and fibrosis toward deep learning becoming central around 2019, then a COVID-19 surge after 2020, and more recently an expansion into clinical management and validation. Citation bursts identified ResNet, U-Net, and Inception as the intellectual backbone of the field. Overall, AI in pneumonia research has rapidly matured, with chest imaging-based deep learning as the core paradigm; future directions point toward rigorous clinical translation, prospective validation, and interdisciplinary integration, while the persistent gap between output and influence across countries underscores the need for strategic collaboration and conceptual innovation. This analysis aims to delineate the quantitative growth patterns, core research themes, intellectual turning points, and collaborative networks that define the global landscape of AI applications in pneumonia research over the past decade.

records.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Cancer: A Comprehensive Review From Basic Research to Clinical Practice.

content.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Cancer: A Comprehensive Review From Basic Research to Clinical Practice.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in oncology, fundamentally shifting cancer care from empirical paradigms to data-driven precision medicine. Modern oncology generates unprecedented volumes of high-dimensional data, including radiomics, digital pathology, and multiomics, which are increasingly harnessed by deep learning architectures like Vision Transformers and U-Nets to characterize tumor phenotypes and heterogeneity. However, despite these algorithmic breakthroughs, critical translational bottlenecks-such as "black box" opacity, cross-institutional batch effects, and the lack of integration into electronic health records-severely impede real-world clinical deployment. This structured narrative review synthesizes the application of multimodal AI frameworks across the entire oncological continuum, from CRISPR-based target discovery and morphological-genomic bridging to reinforcement learning-driven intelligent radiotherapy and clinical decision support systems. We further evaluate emerging paradigms, including federated learning, explainable AI, and patient digital twins, as emerging approaches to address key translational challenges. By bridging the gap between in silico discovery and prospective validation, this review provides a strategic roadmap for the integration of robust, mechanistically transparent AI frameworks. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the potential for AI to deliver dynamic, life-cycle-managed care, supporting the future translation of patient-centered precision oncology into routine clinical practice.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
records.publisher: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

content.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for cerebrovascular digital subtraction angiography: methods, evidence, and challenges.

content.title: Artificial intelligence for cerebrovascular digital subtraction angiography: methods, evidence, and challenges.
content.abstract: Cerebrovascular diseases remain a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) provides high-spatiotemporal-resolution visualization of cerebrovascular anatomy and contrast-agent dynamics and plays an important role in diagnosis, interventional treatment planning, and treatment assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly been applied to cerebrovascular DSA, yet the available evidence is distributed across diverse imaging settings, technical tasks, datasets, and validation strategies. This structured topical review provides a DSA-centered overview of AI-assisted cerebrovascular image analysis across 2D DSA, three-dimensional rotational angiography, and four-dimensional DSA. Literature from Web of Science Core Collection and major engineering databases was screened at title, abstract, and full-text levels using predefined eligibility criteria. The literature is organized around six interconnected tasks: image preprocessing, vessel and lesion segmentation, image registration, reconstruction and generation, disease diagnosis and detection, and hemodynamic analysis. Representative conventional and learning-based methods are reviewed together with their datasets, evaluation metrics, validation designs, and available data or code resources, with particular attention to the strength and limitations of the supporting evidence. Recent studies demonstrate increasing use of spatiotemporal modeling, deep learning, and image-generation techniques, but clinical translation remains constrained by small or single-center datasets, heterogeneous acquisition protocols and evaluation practices, limited external and prospective validation, model interpretability, and deployment requirements. Future work should emphasize acquisition-aware and physics-informed modeling, multicenter and privacy-preserving collaboration, clinically meaningful validation, and closer integration with neurointerventional workflows. By linking methodological developments with their supporting evidence and translational challenges, this review aims to support the development of more robust and clinically applicable AI methods for cerebrovascular DSA.

records.title: Decision-centered artificial intelligence for perioperative care outside the operating room: a practical review for surgeons.

content.title: Decision-centered artificial intelligence for perioperative care outside the operating room: a practical review for surgeons.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across the spectrum of surgical care; however, most existing review articles have organized prior studies primarily by algorithmic type or predicted outcomes. Consequently, a structured understanding of "when" and "why" AI is integrated into real-world clinical workflows, and how its outputs inform surgical decisionmaking, remains insufficiently developed. Although both the preoperative and postoperative phases involve risk prediction, they differ fundamentally in their decision contexts, data characteristics, and modes of clinical application. This review sought to reorganize the surgical AI literature using a decision-centered framework. AI applications during the operation itself-including surgical video analysis, robotic automation, and real-time image guidance-are outside the scope of this review. Instead, this review focuses on AI that supports decision-making before and after surgery, emphasizing decision points relevant to minimally invasive surgical practice, including patient selection, treatment planning, surgical extent and approach planning, postoperative monitoring, discharge readiness, and surveillance planning. This review examined PubMed-indexed studies published between 2015 and 2025, analyzing the literature according to the clinical decision points each study was intended to support, rather than emphasizing comparative model performance. Among the studies reviewed, preoperative AI was predominantly applied to support patient selection and treatment planning in the context of diagnostic uncertainty. In contrast, postoperative AI was mainly used to support time-sensitive management and prognostic assessment. This review reframes surgical AI not as a standalone predictive instrument, but as an integral component of phase-specific clinical decision pathways across the surgical care continuum.

records.title: Using artificial intelligence for food identification and dietary assessment within restaurant and institutional settings: A scoping review.

content.title: Using artificial intelligence for food identification and dietary assessment within restaurant and institutional settings: A scoping review.
content.abstract:
Background

Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have led to greater usage of machine and deep learning approaches to assess dietary intake. However, a comprehensive review of existing approaches used in institutional settings is lacking. The aim of this scoping review is to explore current AI methods being utilized for assessing food selections and dietary intake within these settings and summarize emerging applications of AI methods.

Methods

Literature searches were conducted across four research databases including PubMed, SCOPUS, IEEE Xplore, and Academic Search Premier. Peer-reviewed studies were selected based on the utilization of AI methods to assess food offerings, food selections, or dietary intake collected from human populations within restaurant and institutional settings (i.e., hospitals, schools, or work cafeterias).

Results

After title/abstract and full-text screening, 23 studies met inclusion criteria. Most were conducted in the United States (n = 7). Study settings included hospitals (n = 7), restaurants (n = 6), cafeterias (n = 6), and schools (n = 4). The majority of studies relied on image-based data (n = 21), while some used wearable sensors for collecting dietary data (n = 2). The studies utilized AI for a variety of purposes including policy evaluation (n = 6), dietary assessment (n = 11), and optimization of operations such as billing systems (n = 6). Main challenges for image-based AI methods included dataset variability, overlapping food items, and light reflections.

Conclusions

AI advancements offer the opportunity to more objectively and efficiently measure dietary intake and provide nutritional information, especially within large-scale settings. This demonstrates AI as an emerging tool for public health applications including assessing dietary intake and evaluating policies.

records.title: Diagnostic performance of deep learning models in differentiating benign and malignant pulmonary nodules: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

content.title: Diagnostic performance of deep learning models in differentiating benign and malignant pulmonary nodules: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Lung cancer is the most lethal malignant tumor globally. Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant pulmonary nodules (PNs) is the core of early screening and diagnosis for lung cancer. Deep learning (DL) models can autonomously extract high-dimensional information from medical images, demonstrating technical advantages in this task. Our study systematically evaluates the accuracy and efficacy of DL models in differentiating benign from malignant PNs, providing systematic, high-quality integrated evidence for their diagnostic performance.

Methods

Our study was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA) reporting checklist. We searched the databases of PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science for relevant studies published up to 24 September 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature according to inclusion and exclusion criteria, using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) to assess the risk of bias and applicability of the included studies. The pooled sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of DL models. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression were employed to investigate sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis and publication bias tests were conducted concurrently, and a Fagan plot was generated to assess clinical utility.

Results

A total of 21 retrospective studies were ultimately included. The QUADAS-2 quality assessment indicated that the overall risk of bias in the included studies was manageable. The combined sensitivity, specificity, and AUC of DL models for distinguishing between benign and malignant PNs were 0.92 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.90-0.93], 0.90 (95% CI: 0.86-0.92), and 0.96 (95% CI: 0.94-0.98). The pooled sensitivity and specificity were heterogeneous (I2>75%). A threshold effect test confirmed that no significant threshold effect was observed in our study (Spearman's r=0.221, P=0.336). Subgroup analysis and meta-regression confirmed that model validation method was the primary source of heterogeneity in our study (P=0.00), with cross-validation models demonstrating significantly higher specificity than train-test split models (0.92 vs. 0.84, P=0.00). Models based on the Transformer architecture outperformed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in terms of both sensitivity (0.93 vs. 0.92, P=0.00) and specificity (0.91 vs. 0.89, P=0.00). Sensitivity analysis confirmed the stability of the pooled results, and the funnel plot revealed no significant publication bias (P=0.56). The Fagan plot indicated that at a pretest probability of 50%, the model achieved a positive predictive post-test probability of 90% and a negative predictive post-test probability of only 8%, demonstrating good clinical utility.

Conclusions

DL models demonstrate both high sensitivity and specificity in distinguishing benign from malignant PNs, exhibiting outstanding overall diagnostic performance. With prospective validation and technical optimization in the future, their clinical utility is expected to improve further.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of endoscopy-specific dual-channel supraglottic airways for upper gastrointestinal endoscopic and transesophageal instrumentation procedures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of endoscopy-specific dual-channel supraglottic airways for upper gastrointestinal endoscopic and transesophageal instrumentation procedures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Airway management during upper gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures and other transesophageal instrumentation remains challenging because the airway and procedural device share the upper aerodigestive tract. Endoscopy-specific dual-channel supraglottic airways (dc-SGAs), including the LMA® Gastro™ Airway and the Jcerity Endoscoper™ Airway, are designed to maintain ventilation while permitting passage of an endoscope or transesophageal probe through a separate procedural channel. Nevertheless, their comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain across heterogeneous procedures and comparator strategies.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing endoscopy-specific dc-SGAs with endotracheal tubes, other placed airway or access devices, or non-invasive oxygen therapy during upper gastrointestinal endoscopic or transesophageal instrumentation procedures. Observational studies were summarized narratively but were not included in pooled analyses.

Results

Fifteen studies were included, including 13 randomized controlled trials involving 2,481 participants in the quantitative synthesis and 2 observational studies summarized narratively. Endoscopy-specific dc-SGAs showed comparable first-attempt airway device and endoscope/probe insertion success to comparator strategies and shortened airway device insertion time. Effects on endoscope/probe insertion time and endoscopist satisfaction were inconsistent and varied across comparator types. dc-SGAs reduced intraoperative hypoxemia, mainly in comparisons with non-invasive oxygen therapy. Postoperative sore throat showed a comparator-dependent pattern, with fewer events compared with endotracheal tubes but more events compared with non-invasive oxygen therapy.

Conclusion

Endoscopy-specific dc-SGAs may represent a feasible intermediate airway strategy for selected patients undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopic and transesophageal instrumentation procedures. They may improve airway placement efficiency and, compared with non-invasive oxygen therapy, reduce hypoxemia; however, these potential benefits should be interpreted in light of comparator-dependent throat discomfort, procedure heterogeneity, and the low-to-moderate certainty of evidence.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251182546, identifier [CRD420251182546].

records.title: Impact of metastatic pattern and histologic subtype on PD-(L)1 inhibitor efficacy in HER2-negative advanced gastric and gastroesophageal cancer: a meta-analysis.

content.title: Impact of metastatic pattern and histologic subtype on PD-(L)1 inhibitor efficacy in HER2-negative advanced gastric and gastroesophageal cancer: a meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

The therapeutic benefit of PD-(L)1 blockade in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJ) may vary by niche and tumor biology. We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate how metastatic site and Lauren histologic subtype influence survival outcomes in HER2-negative GC/GEJ treated with PD-(L)1 inhibitor-based chemoimmunotherapy.

Methods

A systematic PubMed, MEDLINE, and Embase search identified phase III randomized controlled trials published between 2021 and 2025 comparing IO plus platinum-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone in HER2-negative metastatic or unresectable GC/GEJ. Hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) were pooled using random-effects models in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population and prespecified subgroups, including liver metastases (LM), peritoneal metastases (PM), Lauren histologic subtype, and PD-L1 expression assessed by combined positive score (CPS) or tumor area positivity score (TAPS). Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic, and analyses were conducted in R.

Results

Six global trials including 5, 410 patients (CHECKMATE 649, ATTRACTION-4, KEYNOTE-859, ORIENT-16, RATIONALE-305, AND GEMSTONE-303) were analyzed. Overall, IO plus CT significantly improved OS compared with CT alone (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.75-0.84; p<0.001). Survival benefit was observed in patients with and without LM (HR 0.75 and 0.82), whereas patients with PM derived limited benefit (HR 0.93). Intestinal-type tumors achieved greater OS improvement than diffuse-type tumors (HR 0.78 vs 0.87). PD-L1 CPS ≥5 predicted superior OS benefit (HR 0.70). Grade ≥3 adverse events were infrequent and hematologic.

Conclusion

First-line chemoimmunotherapy prolongs survival in HER2-negative GC/GEJ. Reduced benefit in diffuse-type and peritoneal disease underscores heterogeneity and supports site- and histology-specific strategies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251174893.

records.title: Risk prediction models for venous thromboembolism among patients with multiple myeloma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Risk prediction models for venous thromboembolism among patients with multiple myeloma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Risk prediction models help identify multiple myeloma (MM) patients at high risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and guide clinical decisions. However, their applicability and accuracy remain unclear. This study aims to systematically review existing VTE risk models in MM patients.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for studies on VTE risk prediction models in patients with MM, up to March 31, 2026. Two investigators independently screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias and applicability of the included studies using the PROBAST tool. Data analysis was performed using the "meta" and "metafor" packages in R software.

Results

A total of 14 studies on VTE risk prediction models in MM patients were included, involving the development and/or validation of seven risk assessment tools. Meta-analysis showed that the overall VTE incidence in MM patients was 7.9% (95% CI [6.2-10.1%]). The combined area under the curve (AUCs) of the seven tools ranged from 0.57 to 0.68, with the IMPEDE VTE and IMPEDED VTE scores showing the best performance. Only two studies used the Hosmer-Lemeshow test for model calibration, and all studies presented the models in formula form. All included studies were at high risk of bias, mainly in the outcome and analysis domains.

Conclusion

Existing VTE risk models for MM patients show low predictive performance (pooled AUC < 0.7) and limited clinical use. Future research should focus on model updating and external validation to improve accuracy and applicability. PROSPERO Registration number ID: CRD420251024346.

records.title: Prevalence and risk factors of depression in patients with diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
