Overall, 24 AI technologies were identified, covering traditional algorithms such as random forest, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbor, as well as deep learning models such as convolutional neural networks, Bidirectional Encoder Representations From Transformers, and ChatGPT. Despite the positive findings, only 21% (3/14) of the studies had entered the clinical validation phase, whereas the remaining 79% (11/14) were still in the exploratory phase of research. Most of the studies (10/14, 71%) were rated as being of moderate methodological quality, with major limitations including lack of a control group, incomplete follow-up data, and inadequate validation systems. In summary, the integrated application of AI in medical questionnaires has significant potential to improve diagnostic efficiency, accelerate scale development, and promote early intervention. Future research should pay more attention to model interpretability, system compatibility, validation standardization, and ethical governance to effectively address key challenges such as data privacy, clinical integration, and transparency.

Background

The World Health Organization reports that >1 billion people worldwide experience mental disorders, with the prevalence of depression and anxiety among children and adolescents at 2.6% and 6.5%, respectively. Methods

The review included peer-reviewed studies that applied AI technologies to medical, psychological, or physiological questionnaires and reported measurable outcomes; non–peer-reviewed, non-English/Chinese, ethically noncompliant, or AI-unrelated studies were excluded. Five databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI) were searched from inception through September 2024. Three independent reviewers conducted data extraction, quality appraisal using the Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and narrative synthesis of AI applications across questionnaire assessment, development, and prediction tasks.

Of 49,091 publications, a total of 14 (0.03%) studies met the inclusion criteria. records.title: The Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery and Development: Implications for Cardiovascular Pharmacology.

content.title: The Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery and Development: Implications for Cardiovascular Pharmacology.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, highlighting the urgent need for more efficient, precise, and cost-effective drug development strategies. Traditional drug discovery pipelines face persistent challenges, including elevated expenses, prolonged timelines, and high attrition rates, particularly with the complex pathophysiology of cardiovascular conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force capable of addressing these barriers across all stages of cardiovascular drug development. This review explores the integration of AI in target identification, compound screening, drug design, pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction, and clinical trial optimization. We highlight state-of-the-art AI tools such as large language models (eg, BioGPT, Geneformer), generative frameworks (eg, Generative Tensorial Reinforcement Learning, Variational Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks), and neural ordinary differential equations, illustrating their ability to accelerate drug discovery, personalize therapy, and improve clinical success rates. In the context of clinical trials, platforms such as Trial Pathfinder have been used to optimize patient recruitment and improve generalizability. Despite these advancements, several challenges persist, particularly those related to data quality, population representativeness, interpretability, and regulatory oversight. Future directions involving the integration of AI with quantum computing, blockchain technology, and precision medicine offer additional opportunities to advance the field. Collectively, these innovations mark a paradigm shift toward faster, safer, and more personalized cardiovascular drug development.

records.title: Role of artificial intelligence in developing predictive models for major adverse cardiovascular outcomes using CCTA adipose tissue characteristics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Role of artificial intelligence in developing predictive models for major adverse cardiovascular outcomes using CCTA adipose tissue characteristics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain as a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide, with coronary artery disease (CAD) and its complications, collectively referred to as major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), necessitating accurate risk stratification. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has emerged as a valuable non-invasive imaging modality, and adipose tissue characteristics derived from CCTA have shown promise as imaging biomarkers for MACE prediction. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the predictive performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven models incorporating CCTA-derived adipose tissue radiomic features for forecasting MACEs. A systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Studies evaluating predictive models developed using different AI algorithms that utilized adipose tissue radiomics as the primary predictor of MACEs in patients undergoing CCTA were included. Model performance was assessed using pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Eleven studies comprising 47 244 participants were included in the analysis. AI-based models integrating adipose tissue radiomic features with clinical data consistently outperformed conventional risk assessment tools, with pooled AUCs ranging from 82.2% to 87.9%. Among the evaluated approaches, deep learning models demonstrated superior predictive performance compared with traditional machine learning and logistic regression-based models. However, considerable heterogeneity (I² > 96%) was observed across studies, reflecting variations in study design, imaging protocols, and AI methodologies. While AI-enhanced CCTA-based adipose tissue characterization demonstrates considerable potential for improving MACE risk prediction, methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation currently restrict its clinical applicability. Future research should prioritize standardized imaging and analytical methodologies, rigorous clinical and external validation, and transparent reporting to facilitate reliable integration of these AI models into routine cardiovascular risk assessment.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in shoulder arthroplasty: latest concepts and clinical integration.
records.publisher: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

content.title: Artificial intelligence in shoulder arthroplasty: latest concepts and clinical integration.
content.abstract:
Background

Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have redefined shoulder arthroplasty, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy, refining surgical planning, and personalizing recovery pathways. However, despite promising technical applications, comparative clinical evidence has not yet demonstrated improved routine surgical or patient outcomes in shoulder arthroplasty.

Review content

Therefore, this review summarizes the state-of-the-art AI applications in shoulder arthroplasty, highlights their strengths and limitations, and outlines integration strategies that align technological innovation with surgical expertise. Preoperatively, deep learning-based imaging, which refers to machine learning methods that use multilayer neural networks to identify complex patterns in imaging data, has shown strong diagnostic performance in detecting rotator cuff tears and glenohumeral arthritis, while AI-assisted three-dimensional reconstruction and anatomy-based modeling help visualize glenoid deformity and support more intuitive preoperative planning, complementing conventional navigation. Intraoperatively, AI-based phase recognition and robotic assistance may enhance component placement precision while also offering potential benefits in surgical training, workflow standardization, and real-time feedback. In addition, emerging innovations such as mixed reality guidance, multimodal integration, and semi-autonomous assistance continue to expand the potential scope of AI applications in shoulder arthroplasty. Postoperatively, machine learning-driven prognostic models and wearable monitoring systems predict complications and guide tailored rehabilitation, supporting earlier risk identification when required. However, current AI systems are unable to capture surgeon intuition and context-dependent expertise. Nevertheless, emerging strategies such as explainable AI, multimodal integration, federated learning, and semi-autonomous surgical platforms aim to bridge these gaps by enhancing transparency, scalability, and clinical trust.

Conclusion

The adoption of AI tools by surgeons depends on their demonstrated reliability across diverse patient anatomies, intraoperative variability, and real-world rehabilitation settings. Thus, technical refinement along with mutual trust with surgeons, supportive regulatory frameworks, and institution-specific implementation strategies are essential for safe integration, particularly because current systems may increase cost, workflow complexity, or delay care when not adequately validated or appropriately implemented.

records.title: Trust in artificial intelligence for diagnosis of dermatologic lesions: a systematic review of qualitative studies.
records.publisher: BMC medical informatics and decision making

content.title: Trust in artificial intelligence for diagnosis of dermatologic lesions: a systematic review of qualitative studies.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) has considerable potential to supports dermatological diagnosis, but its adoption depends on understanding the perspectives of stakeholders. This review aimed to synthesise qualitative evidence on the perceptions, barriers, and facilitators of AI among patients and healthcare professionals.

Methods

We conducted a systematic search of major databases (MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) from database inception through May 26, 2025. Data from ten included qualitative studies were analysed using thematic synthesis. The confidence in each finding was rigorously assessed using the GRADE-CERQual approach.

Results

The synthesis revealed three main themes: (1) the evolving role of AI across the dermatological diagnostic workflow; (2) significant barriers centred on clinical judgment, trust, and the physician-patient relationship; and (3) essential implementation requirements, such as usability and regulation. Confidence in these findings ranged from moderate to high.

Conclusions

Successful AI integration requires transparent, validated, equitable, and usable tools. Stakeholders consistently emphasise that AI should be designed to complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment and the physician-patient relationship to maintain a human-centred focus in medical practice.

Registration

PROSPERO database (CRD420251010095).

records.title: Comparison of the efficacy of neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability in improving exercise-induced fatigue in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Comparison of the efficacy of neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability in improving exercise-induced fatigue in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Exercise-induced fatigue (EIF) is a core problem in competitive sports, significantly affecting the training quality and performance of athletes. Neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability regulation-including both central and peripheral stimulation-offer a novel approach to EIF intervention; however, the comparative efficacy of different techniques remains unclear.

Objective

To compare the effects of various neuromodulation techniques on EIF in athletes using a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, and VIP databases were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials comparing neuromodulation techniques with placebo/sham stimulation/blank control from database inception to June 2026. The Cochrane ROB-2 tool was used to assess risk of bias, and the CINeMA framework was applied to evaluate evidence quality. A Bayesian model was employed for network meta-analysis, with SUCRA values calculated to rank efficacy, and meta-regression was used to explore sources of heterogeneity.

Results

A total of 14 RCTs involving 756 athletes were included. The paired meta-analysis showed that neuromodulation techniques significantly reduced BLA levels and alleviated fatigue (MD = -0.47, 95% CI: -0.57, -0.38). Network meta-analysis indicated that TEAS combined with acupuncture ranked first in improving RPE (SUCRA = 99.3%), blood lactate (SUCRA = 96.3%), and BUN (SUCRA = 72.6%). CINeMA evaluation showed that most evidence was of low quality. Meta-regression revealed that the total number of stimulations negatively moderated the effect on blood lactate (P = 0.001), and intervention type, risk of bias, and study design significantly influenced BUN outcomes (all P < 0.05).

Conclusion

TEAS combined with acupuncture may be associated with the most favorable SUCRA ranking, but this should be interpreted as exploratory for improving EIF in athletes. However, the overall quality of current evidence is low, and SUCRA rankings should be interpreted as exploratory. Future high-quality RCTs are needed to validate these findings and determine the optimal stimulation parameter ranges.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261446854.

records.title: The Future of Antibiotics and Artificial Intelligence: Some Thoughts from Discovery to Bedside.

content.title: The Future of Antibiotics and Artificial Intelligence: Some Thoughts from Discovery to Bedside.
content.abstract: Antibiotic discovery and antibiotic prescribing represent two domains that both stand to benefit from artificial intelligence (AI)-driven progress in the near future. In this article, we discuss these parallel advances and the potential future synergy between AI-enabled antibiotic discovery and AI-assisted antibiotic prescribing. Although multiple challenges remain before these two domains meaningfully converge, their integration could amplify the strengths of each: discovery pipelines generating broader, more diverse classes of antibacterial agents, and prescribing tools capable of matching these agents to individual patients with unprecedented precision. Such a scenario could transform antibiotic therapy by enabling AI-supported, patient-specific treatment decisions while reinforcing the principles of precision medicine and antimicrobial stewardship.

records.title: Environmental memory in macrophages: a PRISMA-guided systematic review and the macrophage environmental memory systems framework.

content.title: Environmental memory in macrophages: a PRISMA-guided systematic review and the macrophage environmental memory systems framework.
content.abstract:
Background

Macrophages respond dynamically to environmental and tissue-derived stressors, but the extent to which these responses constitute persistent environmental memory remains unclear. Studies of trained immunity, epigenetic regulation, non-coding RNAs, transposable elements, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and immunometabolism suggest multiple mechanisms that may contribute to persistent macrophage states, yet these fields have largely developed independently. We therefore systematically evaluated evidence for macrophage environmental memory and used the resulting evidence base to develop the Macrophage Environmental Memory Systems (MEMS) Framework.

Methods

A PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed and Web of Science was completed on 1 August 2026. Searches identified 1,405 records; after removal of 404 duplicates, 1,001 unique records underwent screening. Following title/abstract screening and final evidence audit, 119 primary studies were included. Studies were classified as Direct when a prior stressor induced a macrophage or monocyte molecular or functional state that persisted after removal of the initiating stimulus, was maintained over time or through cell division, or altered the response to a subsequent challenge; Mechanistic when they demonstrated a relevant macrophage or monocyte mechanism without directly establishing persistence or recall; or Contextual when they provided broader mechanistic support. Studies were assigned to six non-mutually exclusive MEMS modules.

Results

Of the 119 included studies, only 4 met the stringent criteria for Direct evidence, whereas 50 were Mechanistic and 65 Contextual, revealing a substantial gap between the extensive literature describing environmentally responsive macrophage mechanisms and evidence directly demonstrating persistent environmental memory. Module assignments overlapped and included transposable element regulation (n = 107), metabolic and signaling reprogramming (n = 86), epigenetic regulation (n = 33), systems integration (n = 17), non-coding RNA regulation (n = 14), and EV-mediated communication (n = 7). The evidence therefore identifies numerous candidate mechanisms that may contribute to the acquisition, maintenance, integration, or communication of persistent macrophage states, while demonstrating that direct evidence of persistence remains limited.

Conclusion

The available literature provides broad mechanistic support for biological processes potentially relevant to macrophage environmental memory but comparatively little direct evidence of persistence or altered subsequent responses. The resulting MEMS Framework organizes this heterogeneous evidence into six interacting molecular systems and is proposed as an evidence-organizing and hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated six-component biological pathway. Prospective exposure-withdrawal, longitudinal, lineage-tracing, perturbational, and rechallenge studies are needed to determine which mechanisms causally establish and maintain persistent macrophage states. The Macrophage-Mediated Molecular Memory (M3) hypothesis represents a downstream, experimentally testable extension of MEMS involving potential communication of environmentally acquired molecular information and remains distinct from evidence establishing the MEMS Framework itself.

records.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy and safety of combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with sertraline for adolescent depression in China.

content.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy and safety of combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with sertraline for adolescent depression in China.
content.abstract:
Background

Adolescent depression is a global health challenge. While selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like sertraline are primary treatments, their efficacy is often limited. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy, neurocognitive impact, and safety of adjunctive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with sertraline in adolescents.

Methods

Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, databases including PubMed (which also covers MEDLINE), Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and Weipu, were searched up to June 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing rTMS plus sertraline versus sertraline monotherapy in adolescents were included. The primary outcomes were depressive symptom reduction (measured by HAMD-17 and HAMD-24) and clinical response rates. Secondary outcomes included cognitive function (Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA) and adverse event.

Results

Twenty-four RCTs (N = 2,155), all conducted in China and published in Chinese, were included. Combination therapy significantly reduced depressive symptoms (HAMD-17: SMD = -1.06; HAMD-24: SMD = -1.39) and improved response rates risk ratio (RR = 1.18). The pooled analysis of three studies suggested that adjunctive rTMS may improve MoCA scores (SMD = 0.99); however, the certainty of evidence was low. The combination group had a slightly higher incidence of mild adverse events (RR = 1.21). Significant heterogeneity (I2>80%) and publication bias were noted; the GRADE certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Meta-regression showed treatment duration did not moderate symptom reduction. Sensitivity analysis identified extreme protocols as the primary source of heterogeneity; excluding them yielded a pooled effect of SMD = -0.74 (I2 = 17%).

Conclusion

Adjunctive rTMS may enhance clinical response and may improve cognitive function in sertraline-treated adolescents, with an acceptable safety profile. The cognitive finding was based on only three studies and low-certainty evidence. Given the very-low-to-moderate GRADE certainty, high heterogeneity, and geographic restriction, the effects may be overestimated. Standardized parameters appear crucial. Future multinational, sham-controlled trials utilizing updated risk-of-bias frameworks are warranted to confirm these findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251118447.

records.title: Malpractice in the machine age: Legal and ethical responses to machine learning in medical imaging.

content.title: Malpractice in the machine age: Legal and ethical responses to machine learning in medical imaging.
content.abstract:
Objectives

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly integrated into diagnostic imaging. This review examines how AI adoption affects malpractice risk, the legal standard of care, liability distribution, and informed consent. It also evaluates regulatory developments and ethical concerns, including explicability, autonomy, and professional accountability.

Key findings

AI-supported image interpretation can improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Its integration is reshaping expectations of reasonable clinical practice, with the potential for negligence claims both when clinicians fail to use validated systems and when they rely on insufficiently tested tools. Liability is uncertain because diagnostic responsibility is distributed across clinicians, healthcare organisations, and developers. Existing negligence frameworks assume human reasoning and struggle to accommodate opaque algorithmic decision-making, limiting courts' ability to assess whether AI-assisted diagnoses meet accepted standards. "Black box" models heighten automation bias, hinder legal scrutiny of error, and complicate professional accountability. Informed consent case law suggests AI involvement should be disclosed when it introduces material differences in risk or outcome, although this remains inconsistently applied. Ethical challenges include threats to patient trust, potential clinician deskilling, and reduced transparency in clinical communication. Regulatory initiatives such as the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation and AI Act move toward clearer governance through requirements for data quality, human oversight, and post-market monitoring, yet explicit malpractice guidance remains under-developed globally.

Conclusion

Traditional legal and ethical frameworks insufficiently address accountability for AI-driven diagnostic errors. Clarifying responsibility, decision authority, and validation requirements is essential to safeguard patient safety and clinician protection.

Implications for practice

Clinical protocols should specify approved use cases, oversight expectations, documentation of AI involvement, and management of clinician-algorithm disagreement. Training should support critical review of outputs to mitigate automation bias.

records.title: Effectiveness of AI and rule-based conversational agents for depression, anxiety and stress: A meta-analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness of AI and rule-based conversational agents for depression, anxiety and stress: A meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Depression, anxiety, and stress are significant global health burdens worsened by restricted access to care. Conversational agents (CAs), encompassing both AI(Artificial Intelligence)- and rule-based systems, provide scalable mental health interventions. This systematic review and meta-analysis analyzed the efficacy of CA interventions in 48 randomized controlled trials covering 28,071 participants. It demonstrated small-to-moderate but significant effects in minimizing symptoms of depression (SMD: -0.27), anxiety (SMD: -0.20), and stress (SMD: -0.26). A Robust Variance Estimation (RVE) approach was used to address within-study dependencies, with results consistent with the random-effects model. Subgroup analyses investigated sources of heterogeneity and indicated greater effects in clinical populations and shorter-duration interventions. Meta-regression identified no appreciable effect of outcome timing. Risk of bias was largely low, although some studies had issues due to missing data or selective reporting. Publication bias was negligible. These results provide evidence for the utilization of conversational agents as effective interventions for lessening psychological symptoms. Additional research is required to evaluate their long-term effectiveness and how best to integrate them into mental healthcare systems.

records.title: Research landscape and emerging themes of ferroptosis in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (2016-2025).

content.title: Research landscape and emerging themes of ferroptosis in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (2016-2025).
content.abstract:
Background

Ferroptosis has received increasing attention as a regulated cell-death process potentially involved in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). However, the structure, development, and thematic evolution of the SA-AKI-ferroptosis literature have not been clearly characterized. This study aimed to map the publication landscape, collaboration patterns, knowledge base, and emerging research themes in this field using bibliometric and science-mapping approaches.

Methods

The Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) was used as the primary bibliometric database, and PubMed was used as an independent sensitivity check. A revised search strategy linked an SA-AKI concept block with a ferroptosis concept block using the Boolean operator AND, without using GPX4, ACSL4, SLC7A11, or other molecular markers as stand-alone search alternatives. Articles and reviews published from 2016 to 2025 were screened for substantive relevance to both SA-AKI and ferroptosis. The final WoSCC corpus was analyzed using VOSviewer 1.6.21 and CiteSpace 6.4. R2 for publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, source co-citation, reference co-citation, clustering, timeline visualization, and burst detection.

Results

Ninety-four WoSCC articles and reviews were assessed for eligibility, of which 68 were included in the final bibliometric corpus. Eligible publications first appeared in 2021 and increased from 2 publications in 2021 to 32 in 2025, with 50 of 68 publications (73.5%) published during 2024-2025. China contributed to 64 of 68 publications, whereas international collaboration remained limited. After keyword harmonization, 23 keywords entered the co-occurrence analysis; the most frequent were "ferroptosis," "acute kidney injury," "sepsis," and "sepsis-associated acute kidney injury," with Nrf2, GPX4, lipid peroxidation, oxidative stress, and related regulatory processes also represented. The reference co-citation network comprised 203 nodes and 858 links and formed 9 clusters (modularity Q = 0.5721; weighted mean silhouette S = 0.8355), connecting the clinical and pathophysiologic literature on SA-AKI with foundational ferroptosis biology and more recent SA-AKI-specific mechanistic studies. The co-cited-source network included 43 sources and 903 links. No sustained reference or keyword bursts were detected using a minimum duration of 2 years; only short 2024-2025 signals emerged in sensitivity analyses using a 1-year minimum duration.

Conclusion

Research on ferroptosis in SA-AKI represents a relatively young and rapidly expanding literature that is highly concentrated geographically and characterized by limited international collaboration. Current knowledge structures link established ferroptosis biology with SA-AKI-specific experimental studies, while recent keyword patterns emphasize oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, Nrf2/GPX4-related regulation, and related cellular processes. The limited duration of citation bursts and the predominance of preclinical literature indicate that the field remains in an early stage of development, and bibliometric signals should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical translation.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome: an updated meta-analysis based on disease severity and treatment strategy subgroups.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome: an updated meta-analysis based on disease severity and treatment strategy subgroups.
content.abstract:
Objective

Sivelestat sodium hydrate is a selective neutrophil elastase inhibitor that attenuates neutrophil-mediated alveolar-capillary injury and is used in some East Asian countries for acute lung injury/ARDS. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and explored whether disease severity, baseline mortality risk, and treatment background modify the mortality effect.

Methods

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to August 27, 2026. Eligible studies were adult studies of sepsis-induced ARDS comparing a sivelestat-containing regimen with an otherwise comparable regimen without sivelestat. COVID-19-only cohorts, non-septic ARDS, mixed-etiology studies without a separable sepsis subgroup, and comparisons in which both groups received sivelestat were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included P/F ratio, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, organ-function scores, inflammatory markers, and adverse events. Mortality was pooled as odds ratios (ORs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood; Hartung-Knapp intervals were used for the primary and study-design analyses. This review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO.

Results

Fourteen studies were eligible for qualitative synthesis, and 10 studies (943 patients) provided extractable 2 × 2 mortality data. Deaths occurred in 73/431 patients receiving sivelestat and 125/512 controls. Sivelestat was associated with lower mortality (OR=0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84; I2 = 0%). The signal persisted in randomized trials (OR=0.37, 95% CI 0.16-0.86; I2 = 0%). Study-level point estimates appeared more favorable in cohorts with baseline P/F < 100 mmHg and control mortality >30%; however, interaction tests were not statistically significant and severity analyses were ecological. Leave-one-out analyses were stable. Egger testing did not detect significant small-study asymmetry (P = 0.197), although power was limited. Baseline-stratified treatment effects by IL-6, PCT, CRP, or neutrophil elastase were unavailable for quantitative effect-modification analyses.

Conclusions

In an updated and etiologically strict evidence synthesis, sivelestat was associated with lower mortality in sepsis-induced ARDS, including in randomized trials. Severe hypoxemia and high baseline risk remain plausible enrichment factors, but current aggregate evidence is insufficient to support a validated phenotype-guided prescribing rule. Co-intervention reporting was sparse, and residual confounding by prone positioning, sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and steroid background cannot be excluded.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO CRD420261541158.

records.title: Dietary modification and nutritional supplements for exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Dietary modification and nutritional supplements for exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Our aim was to evaluate the effects of dietary modification and nutritional supplementation on exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) and the certainty of evidence for each intervention.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through to 1 August 2026. Randomized parallel-group and crossover trials assessing EIB with an exercise challenge, eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea (EVH), or another indirect bronchial provocation test were included. The primary outcome was the maximum or peak percentage fall in forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) within 30 min, with fixed-time-point values treated as proxy outcomes. Comparable intervention-specific effects were synthesized, crossover trials were analyzed as paired designs, and Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) were applied.

Results

A total of 20 studies (22 reports) were included. Low sodium compared with experimentally prescribed high sodium, standard omega-3 fatty acids/fish oil, selected caffeine doses, and PCSO-524 showed potentially favorable signals. However, the evidence was limited by the small sample sizes, proxy outcomes, heterogeneity, risk of bias, missing paired data, or lack of independent replication. Adverse events were inadequately reported.

Conclusion

Current evidence is insufficient to recommend any nutritional intervention for routine prevention or treatment of EIB. Nutritional approaches should not replace guideline-based assessment or pharmacological management.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261485221.

records.title: The effectiveness of dance interventions on sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The effectiveness of dance interventions on sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Sleep health is increasingly recognized as central to physical and mental wellbeing, yet sleep disturbances are common and may be worsened by modern lifestyles. The WHO recognizes dance as a feasible form of physical activity, but evidence for sleep benefits is limited. This meta-analysis quantified the overall and domain-specific effects of dance interventions on sleep quality.

Methods

A systematic search strategy integrating Medical Subject Headings terms and free-text keywords was employed to identify empirical studies investigating the effects of dance interventions on sleep quality across four major English-language databases. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. A meta-analysis was conducted with R 4.5.1 and Stata 18.0, pooling standardized mean differences (SMDs) under a random-effects model. Domain-specific, sensitivity, and subgroup and meta-regression analyses were performed, and publication bias was examined using Begg's and Egger's tests.

Results

10 RCTs (711 participants) were included. Compared with controls, dance significantly improved sleep quality (SMD = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.14-0.82), representing a small-to-moderate effect. At the domain level, only subjective sleep quality remained significant after Holm multiple adjustment, with an effect size of SMD = 0.47. In the sensitivity analysis restricted to studies using the PSQI only, the effect size was attenuated (SMD = 0.355), while heterogeneity decreased substantially (I 2 = 21.7%). No publication bias was detected, and the sensitivity and meta-regression analyses supported the robustness of the findings.

Conclusion

Sleep is an important determinant of individual physical and mental health. Dance interventions, as a nonpharmacological approach, produce a statistically significant overall improvement in sleep quality, with a small-to-approaching-moderate effect that is supported by consistent findings across sensitivity and meta-regression analyses, and with a particularly pronounced improvement in the subjective sleep quality domain. Exploratory subgroup patterns suggested that a group-based aerobic dance program conducted three times per week, 60 min per session, over 12-16 weeks may be associated with greater benefits compared with lower-frequency or shorter-duration dance interventions. In practice, priority should be given to using homogeneous instruments and to standardized reporting of prescription components and adherence, in order to enhance the translational value of the public health evidence.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO, CRD420251104782, available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251104782.

records.title: From microfluidics to nanodelivery: artificial intelligence reshapes neuropharmacology research strategies.

content.title: From microfluidics to nanodelivery: artificial intelligence reshapes neuropharmacology research strategies.
content.abstract: Neurological diseases are characterized by complex etiology, heterogeneity, and significant differences in therapeutic responses, which severely constrain the efficiency of new drug development and the success rate of clinical translation. In recent years, micro- and nanotechnology (micro/nanotechnology) technologies have made breakthroughs in vitro disease modeling, drug delivery, and high-throughput screening, while artificial intelligence (AI) has shown strong advantages in big data analysis, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling, and the deep integration of the two has provided a new technological paradigm for neuropharmacology research. In this review, we systematically review the key applications of micro- and nanotechnology in neuropharmacology, including microfluidic brain chips, nanodelivery systems, and multiscale biosensing platforms, and focus on the central role of AI in drug screening, efficacy assessment, and personalized therapeutic decision-making.

records.title: Blockchain-enabled digital twin systems in healthcare: a systematic scoping review of architectural integration, privacy, governance, ethical challenges, and regulatory solutions under GDPR and HIPAA.

content.title: Blockchain-enabled digital twin systems in healthcare: a systematic scoping review of architectural integration, privacy, governance, ethical challenges, and regulatory solutions under GDPR and HIPAA.
content.abstract:
Background and objective

The integration of blockchain and digital twin (DT) technologies is increasingly recognised as a promising approach for improving healthcare data integrity, interoperability, privacy, and clinical decision support. While digital twins enable dynamic patient modelling and predictive healthcare applications, blockchain provides secure data governance through decentralised trust, auditability, and access control. However, existing research remains fragmented, with limited synthesis of the architectural integration, regulatory readiness, ethical governance, and interoperability of blockchain-enabled healthcare digital twin systems. This systematic scoping review addresses these gaps by providing a comprehensive architectural and compliance-oriented analysis of the current evidence.

Methods

A systematic scoping review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines using Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science. From 148 identified records, 55 eligible studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included after duplicate removal and eligibility screening. Data were extracted on digital twin functionality, blockchain architecture, healthcare application domains, consensus mechanisms, privacy-preserving strategies, and regulatory and ethical alignment. Structured Python-based visual mapping and comparative analyses were performed to identify architectural, governance, and compliance patterns across the literature.

Results

The findings demonstrate that blockchain is predominantly employed to provide access control, audit logging, data integrity, consent management, and secure data provenance within healthcare digital twin ecosystems. Patient-level and EHR-centred digital twins represented the most mature application areas, whereas cross-domain and infrastructure-level frameworks dominated early architectural exploration. The review identifies recurring compliance-oriented architectural patterns while revealing substantial gaps in clinically validated deployments, interoperability with established healthcare standards, decentralised governance models, and formal implementation of GDPR- and HIPAA-compliant engineering practices. Comparative heatmap analyses further highlight the uneven maturity of ethical governance and regulatory integration across blockchain functionalities.

Conclusion

This review provides the first comprehensive compliance-oriented architectural synthesis of blockchain-enabled healthcare digital twin systems by integrating technical architecture, regulatory readiness, ethical governance, and privacy-preserving design patterns within a unified analytical framework. The proposed architectural mapping identifies critical research gaps in interoperability, governance engineering, consensus optimisation, and real-world clinical validation, providing a foundation for the development of trustworthy, GDPR/HIPAA-aligned, FHIR-compatible, and clinically interoperable healthcare digital twin ecosystems.

records.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Dell'Avanzi, FG, Enes, A, Alves-Marques, F, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Bello, G, Seima, G, Nass, G, Moreira, NF, Santana, C, Mohan, AE, Piñero, A, Schoenfeld, BJ, and Souza-Junior, TP. Dumbbell bench press and dumbbell fly elicit similar pectoralis major muscle hypertrophy in recreationally trained men. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Exercise selection is one of the main resistance training (RT) variables for eliciting inhomogeneous muscle growth. Whether exercises that differ in resistance moment arm elicit whole- and nonuniform hypertrophy of the pectoralis major remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of the dumbbell bench press (DBP) and dumbbell fly (DFLY) on pectoralis major muscle thickness (MT). Twenty-six young healthy men (RT experience 3.3 ± 3.1 years) were allocated to DBP or DFLY groups, training twice a week over a 10-week period. The weekly set number was individualized according to subjects' previous RT pectoralis major volume. Pectoralis major MT was assessed by ultrasound imaging at medial (30%), intermediate (50%), and lateral (70%) sites at baseline and postintervention. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect for time (p < 0.05) but no time-by-group interaction for the medial site (p = 0.500), intermediate site (p = 0.864), lateral site (p = 0.720), and the sum of the MT across sites (p = 0.985). Therefore, both exercises elicited similar general and regional hypertrophy on pectoralis major MT in recreationally trained individuals. Coaches and practitioners can select DBP or DFLY when targeting pectoralis major muscle development in recreationally trained men based on personal preference and goals within the RT program.

records.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
content.abstract:
Background

Dietary protein supplements are commonly consumed to support increases in lean body mass among healthy adults engaged in resistance training (RT). Although whey protein has been extensively investigated, plant-based protein supplements have emerged as a viable alternative for individuals who avoid animal-derived products.

Methods

The present study aims to evaluate, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, the effects of plant-based versus whey protein supplementation on body composition in untrained adults (18-59 years) undergoing RT, using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA). The systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251145410). Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, identifying 5 studies that met the inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis.

Results

When combined with RT, both plant-based and whey protein supplementation were associated with improvements in lean body mass (LBM) and body fat mass (BFM), with no significant between-group differences observed.

Conclusions

Thus, soy- and pea-based protein supplements may support favorable body composition changes in adults initiating RT and could be considered practical nutritional options for individuals seeking alternatives to whey protein. Regarding chia-based protein, the available evidence is currently limited to a single study that did not demonstrate significant changes in lean body mass; therefore, firm conclusions regarding its efficacy cannot be drawn at this time.

records.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Enes, A, Macedo, ACG, Nass, G, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Alves-Marques, F, Santana, C, Dell'Avanzi, FG, Rodrigues, BG, Alves, RC, De Souza, EO, and Souza-Junior, TP. How often should volume increase? Effects of different volume-progression frequencies on strength and hypertrophy adaptations in females. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Resistance training (RT) volume is an important programming variable for strength and hypertrophy. However, how frequently RT volume should be progressed remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the effects of progressively increasing RT volume by 2 weekly sets targeting the quadriceps femoris every 2 weeks (2 W) or every 4 weeks (4 W) over a 12-week period in recreationally trained women. Using a within-subject design and accounting for previous RT volume, 21 subjects (age 23.3 ± 3.9 years; RT experience 1.1 ± 0.7 years) had their limbs assigned to one of the 2 conditions: 2 weeks (2 W) or 4 weeks (4 W). 45° leg-press 1-repetition maximum (1RM) and the sum of muscle thickness (∑MT) of the proximal (30%), middle (50%), and distal (70%) portions of the lateral thigh were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect of time for 1RM (p < 0.0001), with no difference between the 2 and 4 W conditions (p = 0.317). Similarly, regarding the ∑MT, the analysis indicated a main effect of time (p < 0.001), with no difference between the conditions (p = 0.616). Within the relatively high training volumes examined, progressing the RT volume by 2 weekly sets every 2 or 4 weeks did not elicit detectable differences in strength and hypertrophy adaptations over 12 weeks in recreationally trained women.

records.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

records.title: Citrulline Malate Ingestion Enhances Muscular Performance During a Selected Hypertrophy Hack Squat Training Protocol.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Citrulline Malate Ingestion Enhances Muscular Performance During a Selected Hypertrophy Hack Squat Training Protocol.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Wax, B, Dorgo, S, Montalvo, S, Lyons, B, and Mayo, JJ. Citrulline malate ingestion enhances muscular performance during a selected hypertrophy hack squat training protocol. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined potential ergogenic effects of an oral citrulline malate supplement (CM) during lower-body resistance training. Fifteen resistance-trained men completed a randomized, counterbalanced, double-blind crossover design. Subjects ingested 8.0 g CM or placebo 60 minutes before 8 sets of hack squats at 67% one-repetition maximum to failure with 90-second recovery intervals, repeating the protocol with the alternate treatment 1 week later. Blood lactate before and after exercise, rating of perceived exertion after sets 4 and 8, muscle soreness at 24 and 48 hours, and heart rate and blood pressure at rest and 5 and 10 minutes after exercise were assessed. Hack squat repetition numbers were higher overall in the CM condition (condition effect p = 0.0213), and CM increased total repetitions by 10.7 (95% confidence interval 1.4 to 20.0; p = 0.0265; Hedges' g = 0.61) and total workload by 1,064.7 units (95% confidence interval 84.1 to 2045.4; p = 0.0354; Hedges' g = 0.57). Blood lactate increased after exercise but did not differ by condition. Rating of perceived exertion showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted set-specific difference. Citrulline malate was associated with significantly lower muscle soreness overall and at both 24 and 48 hours after exercise. Heart rate and systolic blood pressure showed condition × time interactions, with Holm-adjusted CM vs. placebo differences at 5 minutes after exercise, whereas diastolic blood pressure showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted time-point difference. Acute CM supplementation may improve lower-body resistance training work capacity and reduce perceived soreness without altering lactate accumulation or perceived exertion.

records.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Chilingirian-Padrón, R, Álvarez-Yates, T, and García-García, O. Effects of in-season contrast strength training on jump performance and sprint ability in female field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 6-week in-season contrast strength training program incorporating sport-specific tasks on neuromuscular performance in sub-elite female field hockey players. Twenty-five athletes completed a pre-post single-cohort intervention integrated into their regular team schedule. Each session consisted of 3 sequential blocks: (a) a high-load strength exercise targeting maximal strength or hypertrophy (70-85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]); (b) a biomechanically related explosive action performed at low load (∼30% 1RM) and high execution velocity; and (c) a high-speed sport-specific task. Jump performance was assessed using bilateral and unilateral countermovement jumps (CMJs) and free arm CMJ, whereas sprint ability was evaluated through 10- and 20-m sprints. A mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to determine the effects of the intervention, with Time (Pre, Post) as within-subject factor and Playing Position (defenders, midfielders, forwards) as between-subject factor, with the level of significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements were observed in all jump and sprint assessments: jump performance increased by 5.7-29.6%, whereas sprint ability improved by 1.6-1.9%. These findings indicate that 6 weeks of contrast strength training incorporating high-speed sports-specific tasks performed during the competitive season elicited meaningful improvements in stretch-shortening cycle-related jump performance and sprint ability in sub-elite female field hockey players.

records.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Petisco-Rodríguez, C, Barroso-Hernández, Á, Bartolomé-Sánchez, I, and Crego, A. Comparative effects of resistance training and high-intensity interval training on body composition, metabolic health, and functional strength in overweight and obese adults: A 12-week randomized controlled trial. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to compare the effects of 2 training programs on anthropometric and physiological variables in overweight and obese adults. Ninety subjects (age = 39.9 ± 10.4 years; body mass index (BMI) = 31.0 ± 4.3 kg·m-2) were randomly assigned to a resistance training group (RG; n = 30), a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) group (HG; n = 30), or a nontraining control group (CG; n = 30). Both the RG and HG performed 2 weekly sessions for 12 weeks. The RG completed 8 upper-body and lower-body resistance exercises at 70% of 1 repetition maximum, while the HG performed high-intensity intervals at 80% of the maximum heart rate. A 3 (group: CG, RG, HG) × 2 (time: pre, post) mixed ANOVA revealed significant effects on the BMI, body fat, and fasting glucose. Both training groups showed similar improvements in all measures from preintervention to postintervention. Compared with CG, RG and HG had reduced body fat and BMI, while RG demonstrated greater gains in muscle mass, fasting glucose, and grip strength. Paired t-tests confirmed significant within-group improvements in BMI, body fat, grip strength, and fasting glucose in the RG and HG. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.017 after the Bonferroni correction. These findings suggest that both resistance training and HIIT enhance the body composition of overweight and obese adults. However, resistance training may provide additional benefits in muscular fitness and glycemic control, supporting its role as a practical strategy for improving metabolic health in this population.

records.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Sebastian-Rico, JM, Muñoz-Fernández, MJ, Martínez-Aranda, LM, Calvo-Lluch, Á, and Ortega-Becerra, M. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training in women soccer players and its relationship with quality of life and pelvic floor muscle strength: a randomized controlled pilot study. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study investigated the effects of a 6-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program on muscle strength, function, and the prevalence of related dysfunctions in professional female soccer players using a randomized controlled pilot study design. Twenty nulliparous professional soccer players from the Spanish professional league (2024-2025 season) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 8). Assessments included anthropometric data, validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form and Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), clinical interviews, and physical examination using the PERFECT method and manometry. The intervention consisted of a 6-week supervised PFMT program (4 sessions/week, 30 minutes each) progressed through 4 phases: education, proprioception, strengthening, and functional integration. Results showed significant group × time interactions for pelvic floor self-efficacy (Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), with scores in the PFMT group increasing by 48.8 and 59.6% (p < 0.05), representing large between-group effect sizes (d = 0.91-1.26). Pelvic floor muscle performance increased by 122.4% in the intervention group (d = 1.25), whereas no meaningful changes were observed in the control group. No adverse events were reported. In conclusion, a 6-week supervised PFMT program is an effective and safe intervention for professional female soccer players, significantly improving muscle function and self-efficacy. These findings support the integration of PFMT for both therapeutic and preventive purposes in elite, high-impact sports environments.

records.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Campos, BT, Rodrigues, JGdS, Cal Abad, CC, Bachi, ALL, dos Santos, CMM, Tritto, AC, Kons, RL, Penna, EM, and Prado, LS. Performance and physiological responses to strength training programs in elite judo athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study compared the effects of 2 short-term strength training models, block planning (BP) and undulating planning (UP), on performance, physiological, and perceptual responses in elite judo athletes. We hypothesized that BP would induce greater physiological strain due to the concentration of training stimuli. Eighteen judokas (14 men and 4 women) were randomly assigned to BP (n = 9) or UP (n = 9) for 4 weeks, performing 6 weekly strength sessions alongside technical-tactical training. Performance outcomes included countermovement jump (CMJ), muscle power (back squat and bent-over row), and the Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT). Monitoring variables included internal load, heart rate variability (HRV), and well-being, while physiological markers included creatine kinase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and cortisol. Data were analyzed using 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA (p < 0.05). Both groups improved SJFT performance (p < 0.01), with no between-group differences. Block planning increased lower-limb peak power (p = 0.01; d = 0.90), whereas UP showed no meaningful change. Upper-limb power and CMJ did not change in either group. Internal load showed different temporal patterns between models. Block planning presented higher HRVcv values (p = 0.04), indicating greater autonomic perturbation. Creatine kinase and TNF-α increased over time in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while cortisol showed an interaction without clear post hoc differences. In conclusion, BP improved lower-limb power but increased physiological strain, whereas UP elicited similar judo-specific improvements with lower recovery demands. These findings highlight the importance of training organization for balancing performance and recovery in elite judo athletes.

records.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
content.abstract:
Background

High-protein diets have consistently been associated with favorable changes in body composition in both sedentary and exercise-trained populations. Despite abundant evidence supporting protein intakes above the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for active individuals, the effects of deliberate protein overfeeding, particularly in those already consuming adequate protein, remain incompletely characterized. The primary purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition in exercise-trained men and women. The secondary purpose was to determine whether body composition adaptations differed by FTO rs9939609 genotype.

Methods

Fifty-six exercise-trained men and women (age: 22.40 ± 5.78 years; body mass: 75.47 ± 14.98 kg; BMI: 24.52 ± 3.50 kg/m2; resistance training: 5.12 ± 3.35 h/week) were enrolled in a 4-week dietary intervention. Participants were instructed to increase their daily protein intake by approximately 20% above baseline while maintaining habitual training. Body composition was assessed pre- and post-intervention using a multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device (InBody® 270). Dietary intake was self-monitored via MyFitnessPal®. Thirty-five participants completed both pre- and post-testing assessments and constituted the primary analysis. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values indicated that FTO genotype was not a significant predictor of body composition changes (p > 0.05).

Results

Protein intake trended toward a significant increase over the 4-week period (pre: 146 ± 66 g/day vs. post: 164 ± 79 g/day; p = 0.053), representing an approximate 12% increase. Total energy intake, carbohydrate, and fat intake did not significantly change. Lean body mass increased significantly (pre: 59.95 ± 14.14 kg vs. post: 60.62 ± 14.42 kg; p = 0.005; Cohen's d = 0.31) and total body water increased significantly (pre: 43.85 ± 10.35 L vs. post: 44.34 ± 10.55 L; p = 0.005). Fat mass (p = 0.424), body fat percentage (p = 0.149), and total body mass (p = 0.09) did not significantly change.

Conclusions

A 4-week modest protein overfeeding protocol in exercise-trained men and women was associated with a significant increase in lean body mass and total body water without concomitant increases in fat mass. These adaptations were not modified by FTO rs9939609 genotype. These findings support the contention that higher protein intakes do not promote fat accretion and may facilitate improvements in body composition in trained individuals.

records.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
content.abstract:
Purpose

The primary purpose of this study was to investigate whether isometric resistance training (RT) leads to reticulospinal tract (RST) adaptations.

Methods

A "RT group" of 30 healthy adults completed 4 weeks (15 sessions) of volume-matched unilateral elbow flexion RT involving high (32 repetitions/session at 70% maximal voluntary torque [MVT]) or low (64 repetitions/session at 35%MVT) loads. An additional 15 participants served as controls (CON group). Pre- and post-test MVT, RST properties (RST gain ratio derived from the StartReact assessment; startling auditory stimulus-conditioned/control motor evoked potential [MEP] ratio; and startling stimulus-conditioned/control cervicomedullary MEP [CMEP] ratio), CST excitability and intracortical inhibition properties (in response to transcranial magnetic stimulation) were assessed.

Results

MVT increased more in the RT group (+12.8%; n = 30) vs. CON group (-4.3%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), p = 0.001). However, changes in RST properties assessed using a series of indirect measures did not differ between the RT group (-1.4% to 6.6%; n = 30) and CON group (-4.5% to 10.5%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), 0.352 ≤ p ≤ 0.834).

Conclusions

RST adaptations within a sample of healthy young men and women, assessed using various indirect measurement approaches, did not occur following only 4 weeks of isometric elbow flexion RT. These findings add to the currently limited scientific evidence from short-term human RT intervention studies available to inform the use of RT for healthy individuals or patients primarily targeting the development of RST function.

records.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
content.abstract:
Purpose

The present study aimed to evaluate associations between resistance training and binge drinking in relation to musculoskeletal composition, physical fitness, cognitive function, and psychological wellness in young adult females.

Methods

Participants were categorized into four groups: sedentary low alcohol consumers (SL; n=12), sedentary binge drinkers (SB; n=12), resistance-trained low alcohol consumers (RTL; n=12), and resistance-trained binge drinkers (RTB; n=12). Measurements included body composition via DEXA scan, muscle quality via ultrasonography, and insulin sensitivity via oral glucose tolerance test. Physical performance was assessed using maximum chair stand power, vertical jump, broad jump, knee extensor torque, grip strength, and push-ups to failure. Tests and questionnaires were used to assess cognitive function and psychological wellness.

Results

Resistance-trained females had lower body fat than sedentary females (RTL = 29.28±4.27%; RTB = 29.03±3.67%; SL = 37.18±5.32%; SB = 34.83±3.54%; p<0.05), and RTL had more fat-free mass than SL and SB (RTL = 48.31±5.81 kg; SL = 38.08±6.59 kg; SB = 40.37±6.05 kg; both p<0.05). There were no differences between RTL and RTB in bone mineral density, muscle quality, or physical performance. RTL outperformed SL and SB on vertical jump (both p<0.05) while RTB outperformed SL and SB on broad jump. RTL had lower fasting blood glucose than RTB (88.92±12.09 mg/dL and 103.17 ± 10.21 mg/dL, respectively; p=0.008), and lower postprandial blood glucose than all groups (RTL = 103.83±19.82 mg/dL; RTB = 137.58±21.54 mg/dL; SL = 148.50±44.60 mg/dL; SB = 139.25±14.49 mg/dL; all p<0.05).

Conclusions

The results suggest that ≥1 year of binge drinking is associated with poorer metabolic health without differences in performance in young females. Further, frequent RT may mitigate the effects of binge drinking on body composition.

records.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
content.abstract:
Background

High protein intake is common among resistance-trained athletes, but its association with renal biomarkers across different exercise modalities remains uncertain. This study investigated whether consuming a high-protein diet (3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹) during 16 weeks of resistance training (RT) or concurrent training (CT) affects renal biomarkers and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in resistance-trained men.

Methods

Forty-eight resistance-trained men (26 ± 6 years; BMI 25.6 ± 2.9 kg·m⁻²) were randomized to 16 weeks of RT or CT (4 sessions·wk⁻¹) while consuming either 1.6 or 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ of protein in a 2 × 2 factorial design. Forty-four participants with complete pre- and post-intervention data were analyzed. Fasting blood samples were assessed for blood urea nitrogen (BUN), BUN/creatinine ratio, cystatin C, and eGFR calculated using the CKD-EPI creatinine (2021), cystatin C (2012), and creatinine-cystatin C (2021) equations. Within-group changes were evaluated using paired t-tests, and factorial effects were assessed using linear mixed-effects models (Time × Training × Protein).

Results

No statistically significant Time × Protein or Time × Training × Protein interactions were detected for any renal biomarker or eGFR estimate (all p ≥ 0.182). No significant within-group changes occurred in the 1.6 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups (all p > 0.05). In both 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups, BUN and cystatin C increased (all p ≤ 0.017), while eGFR estimates decreased (all p ≤ 0.009). The BUN/creatinine ratio remained unchanged (p ≥ 0.614). However, these within-group findings were descriptive because the corresponding interaction effects were not statistically significant.

Conclusions

In resistance-trained men, 16 weeks of high protein intake did not produce statistically detectable differences in renal biomarker or eGFR changes compared with moderate protein intake, irrespective of training modality. Although modest increases in BUN and cystatin C and small decreases in eGFR estimates were observed within the high-protein groups, these findings were not supported by significant factorial interactions. The limited sample size precludes excluding clinically meaningful differences, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

records.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
content.abstract:
Background

Emerging evidence links movement behaviors to vitamin D status. This study investigated associations between physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep with vitamin D status and explored sex differences in these relationships.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 3195 adults (49.1 ± 17.1 years, 45.5% males) from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete data. Self-reported PA, SB, and sleep duration were assessed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Generalized linear and logistic regression models were performed.

Results

SB was negatively associated with vitamin D levels in the whole sample (β = -0.006; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.012, -0.001) and males (β = -0.008; 95% CI: -0.014, -0.002), but not females. Sleep duration was positively associated with vitamin D among males only (β = 0.023; 95% CI: 0.003, 0.043). Meeting both PA and SB guidelines showed the strongest and most consistent association with vitamin D sufficiency, observed across the whole sample (odds ratio [OR] = 2.129; 95% CI: 1.504, 3.012), males (OR = 2.013; 95% CI: 1.021, 3.967), and females (OR = 2.214; 95% CI: 1.360, 3.605).

Conclusions

Movement behaviors demonstrate independent and joint associations with vitamin D status in US adults, with modest sex-specific patterns that warrant replication. Combined adherence to PA and SB guidelines was consistently associated with greater odds of vitamin D sufficiency across sexes.

records.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Dark chocolate (DC) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for exercise performance and recovery, but evidence in trained women remains limited. This exploratory secondary analysis examined selected lower-limb performance outcomes and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in female CrossFit® athletes.

Methods

This secondary analysis included 15 trained female CrossFit® athletes from a randomized crossover trial. No separate a priori sample-size calculation was performed for these outcomes (minimum detectable paired effect, d_z = 0.78). DC (30 g/day, 85% cocoa), placebo chocolate (PLA), and an open-label control (CONN) were compared at four operationally defined menstrual-cycle assessments after three days of supplementation. DC-PLA allocation was blinded, but blinding success was not assessed. Outcomes were vertical jump height (VJH), knee isokinetic and isometric performance, and muscle-specific DOMS after the Cindy WOD.

Results

Condition effects survived FDR control for VJH and 19 of 22 dynamometry outcomes. Across assessments, VJH was 34.48 ± 5.09 cm with DC and 30.22 ± 2.34 cm with PLA (mean difference 4.27 cm, 95% CI 1.45 to 7.08; Holm-adjusted p = 0.017; g_av = 1.09). No condition-by-assessment interaction survived FDR control (all q ≥ 0.141). DOMS showed significant time effects for all three muscles, peaked at approximately 24 h, remained elevated at 48 h, and declined toward baseline by 72 h. A condition-by-time effect remained significant only for gastrocnemius soreness (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012; ηp2 = 0.212); no DOMS condition main effect or condition-by-assessment-by-time interaction was supported.

Conclusion

DC was associated with higher values for selected lower-limb outcomes, but these exploratory findings do not establish phase-specific efficacy, equivalent effects across cycle assessments, or a consistent DOMS benefit. Unusually large performance estimates and unmodeled period and carryover effects warrant caution.

records.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Healthy aging is a priority for many individuals; however, a decline in physical function and poor body composition are common age-related changes that can cause the added years from rising life expectancy to be spent in poor health. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms involved in aging has become increasingly important, including the role of phospholipids (PLs) and how age-related changes in PL content may interfere with lipid metabolism and normal functioning of the musculoskeletal system. Milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) is a bovine milk fraction rich in PLs that may have the potential to support good physical health, so that quality of life can rise alongside life expectancy.

Methods

This narrative review was based on a literature search conducted on Google Scholar, PubMed, and Scopus in May 2026 using the following keywords and Boolean operators: milk fat globule membrane OR MFGM AND physical function OR body composition OR older adults. Studies were included if they were randomized clinical trials (RCTs) investigating MFGM's effects on physical function and/or body composition in older adults.

Results

Findings suggest that MFGM supplementation, when consumed in conjunction with exercise, is an effective way to improve physical function in older adults, particularly among Japanese cohorts; however, changes in habitual diet in response to exercise, variable PL concentrations, and other added ingredients used in interventions may have influenced these results. In contrast, its effects on body composition appear more modest, with some studies reporting no benefits, especially when exercise was not part of the study design, or when compliance may have been a factor.

Conclusions

Beyond the combined use of supplementation and exercise, future RCTs should consistently report participant compliance and, where possible, examine MFGM as a standalone intervention to distinguish its effects from other bioactive ingredients. Greater standardization is also needed, particularly regarding PL dose. Studies should also aim to include participants from more diverse ethnic backgrounds to capture a wider range of physiological responses and improve generalizability of the findings.
